title: CLO 2025.2 - Introduction to Other Features
description: CLO 2025.2 Overview of Other New Features! Join CLO technical experts to explore all the remaining feature enhancements in the new version, helping to elevate your design workflow to the next level!
transcript:
In version 2025.2, we have introduced a major update to the new drawing library.  
In the previous version, the new drawing library could only exist as a floating window, but in version 2025.2, both options are available.  
You can keep the original form of the drawing library, or you can dock it to the side of the column.  
After clicking the drawing library icon, the drawing library will open randomly as a floating window.  
To dock the drawing library, click the docking icon in the upper right corner of the drawing library. The drawing library will automatically dock to the left side of the screen column.  
You can also choose to dock the drawing library on the right side of the column.  
The window and property editor are displayed in a row. If you want to remove docking and restore the floating window, simply click the window icon in the upper right corner of the drawing library.  
Once you have docked or undocked the drawing library, this user setting will be saved and will automatically apply the next time you start the software.  
This feature allows Clo to adapt to different workflows and help users customize their user interface.  
Additionally, with the update to the new drawing library, the original old drawing library will be removed.  

In the new version, we have updated the user customization settings.  

In the new version, we have applied a new shortcut unlocking feature.  
After opening the user customization window settings, you can use the unlock option in the shortcut selection tab.  
This lock feature also supports searching by order name and shortcut.  
You can directly enter a keyword or the full name to search for shortcut keys.  
Then press the corresponding keyboard shortcut to identify it.  
If you want to customize the shortcut, please try to avoid default system shortcut conflicts.  
If there is a shortcut conflict, a window will appear allowing you to choose whether to replace it.  
This new unlock function can save your time.  
It is highly effective when searching for specific tools, menu shortcuts, or getting shortcut options.  

Version 2025.2 has made a major update to shortcut codes.  
Users can now directly view and edit all shortcuts in the 2D window.  
The sewing lines will also be linked to shortcuts to ensure the structure remains consistent.  
In the 2D window, you can see the shortcuts on the codeboard.  
They automatically adapt in size and are displayed across all sizes.  
Switch to the edit code tool.  
After selecting a shortcut, you can adjust its position in the property editor.  
Click on the fixed size to lock the shortcut code position.  
This ensures the shortcut position matches the codeboard and remains unchanged across all other sizes.  
Open the length display line in the 2D window.  
When switching sizes, you will see the distance between shortcuts remains constant.  
If you need to modify it while keeping the distance to another shortcut unchanged,  
use the shortcut tool to select the shortcut.  
In the property editor, click lock.  
The lock position can be changed from the start point to the end point.  
You can also enter a number to adjust the distance.  
Keep the original distance unchanged here.  
Switch to other sizes.  
You will see the length of the other endpoint remains unchanged.  
Now we will unlock it.  
Switch back to the edit code tool.  
If further editing is needed, you can manually enter numbers in the table according to the actual situation.  
Please note the input value is always calculated based on the machine code.  
If you need to reverse the direction of a specific size, add a comma before the number.  
If you want to reverse all sizes, you can select the opposite direction.  
Use the edit sewing line tool to switch to other sizes.  
You can see the sewing lines of the chest coat and skirt whiteboard.  
If you need to edit the direction of a specific size, add a comma before the number.  
The sewing lines of the chest coat and skirt whiteboard are always perfectly aligned at the cutout.  
This update links sewing lines and cutouts across all sizes.  
Therefore, when switching sizes of the chest coat, the sewing lines will always follow the cutout.  
This optimization improves the accuracy of measurements and the overall board consistency.  

In Clo 2025.2, based on accurate 2D measurement, sticker placement becomes more convenient.  
Use the adjustment sticker tool to select the sticker that needs adjustment.  
In the property editor, you can activate the 2D measurement function based on the endpoint or the outer line.  
This function operates on the endpoint.  
First, select it at the bottom.  
Then you will see a distance parameter at the bottom.  
Its measurement value will be displayed next to the sticker within the sheet range.  
Through this method, you can manually enter values to accurately control the distance between the endpoint or the outer line of the sticker.  
For the back position, activate the option on the outer line of the sheet.  
Enter the specified distance here to accurately locate the sticker, fully meeting process unit requirements.  
This update makes sticker positioning more accurate, ensuring the final design is under your control.  

In version 2025.2, we updated the selection option of the fixing needle tool.  
Now you can delete all fixing needles on the selected sheet.  
Use the fixing needle tool to add fixing needles randomly to different sheets.  
Select any fixing needle, right-click, and delete the fixing needles on the selected sheet.  
In previous versions, when selecting fixing needles on a sheet, there were only two options:  
delete the selected fixing needles, or delete all fixing needles.  
Now, you can delete all fixing needles on the selected sheet without deleting all fixing needles on the entire garment.  
This update provides greater flexibility for creating 3D garments.  
Right-click a fixing needle on any sheet side and delete the fixing needles on that sheet.  
Note that this fixing needle may involve multiple sheets.  
With this new function, fixing needles do not need to be deleted for the whole set but can be deleted sheet by sheet.  
Switch to the selection tool.  
Select any fixing needle that involves two sheets.  
Double-click the fixing needle.  
Press the Delete key to remove fixing needles on this sheet.  
Double-clicking selects all fixing needles on the same sheet.  
Press Delete to remove all fixing needles on that sheet.  
You can also use the previous function to delete all fixing needles.  
We hope this update gives you more options when editing fixing needles on 3D garments.  

In version 2025.2, you can choose whether to activate sewing.  
Open the sewing tool.  
Add a sewing line to the neckline or create a random sewing line on the garment.  
Find the activation option in the property editor.  
Open simulation.  
Re-select the activated sewing line.  
Simulate again.  
In previous versions, once sewing was applied, it always existed unless deleted.  
In this version, the sewing function has been updated.  
After adding sewing in the armhole, you can choose to deactivate it.  
Activate or deactivate the sewing option.  
Set the tool on the virtual model.  
You can also apply the activation option similarly on the virtual model.  
Add sewing effects at any position on the virtual model.  
Find the activation option in the property editor.  
Open simulation.  
Re-select the activated sewing line.  
Simulate again.  
We hope this update makes sewing functions more flexible.  

In previous versions, only CPU simulation supported software model simulation.  
After this update, software model simulation can also be used in GPU simulation mode.  
Click the virtual model.  
In the property editor, find and activate the software model simulation option.  
The 3D window at the bottom right will display the software model simulation icon.  
When switching from simulation mode to GPU mode and re-simulating,  
you will see the virtual model simulated as a software model.  
Recording software model animation in the animation editor will speed up your recording.  
Please note this function is only supported on Windows systems with NVIDIA GPUs.  
We hope this update provides a faster and smoother experience.  

In version 2025.2, you can customize hats as configurations.  
Find the virtual model in the main menu.  
Select customized configuration.  
In the pop-up window, when selecting configuration type, the hat option has been added.  
As before, you can import OBJ files.  
You can also customize versions as hats.  
Select all versions of the hat.  
After completing other option settings, click Save.  
Save it as a customized configuration.  
Close the prompt window.  
After customization, you can freely add hats to other projects.  
We hope the new configuration type helps you explore more possibilities.  

From version 2025.2, MetaHuman can be imported as a virtual model in the UI.  
You can import MetaHuman in the main menu column in DNA format.  
Before importing, please ensure your DNA file is stored in the same path as other postage files to ensure correct skin presentation.  
In the MetaHuman DNA import window, click the File plus icon.  
Select the corresponding MetaHuman body and head files.  
You can modify various settings in the import window, such as unit and proportion.  
By default, the system will automatically add arrangement points and create a test fitting.  
You can also deselect these options to manually add arrangement points and create a test fitting later.  
After clicking OK, MetaHuman will be added to the workspace and can be used as a virtual model.  
In the 3D vertical menu, you can modify the surface type of the model under virtual model information display.  
Click on display arrangement points to show MetaHuman’s arrangement points.  
We wish you a smooth version rollout.  
This function supports import of self-defined role models created by MetaHuman Creator, further improving compatibility between Clo and Unreal Engine.  

In version 2025.2, pull chains can be copied to versions with symmetrical relationships.  
Right-click on a pull chain, select copy to version with symmetrical modification.  
The pull chain will be copied to the opposite side.  
The copied pull chain maintains consistent material and specifications as the original.  
This function improves work efficiency and quickly creates symmetrical pull chains.  

In the new version, we optimized the appearance of pull chains, pull heads, and costume pull-outs.  
Now pull chains can be activated with the version or back-activated.  
This makes operation more convenient.  
When back-activating the related version, the pull chain remains in the same state.  
When back-activating the version again, the pull chain will also activate.  
We hope this simplifies operation and improves work efficiency.  

Version 2025.2 supports rotating text in the text editor, both horizontally and vertically.  
No need for manual rotation.  
To rotate text vertically or horizontally, select it and click the corresponding rotate button.  
You can see the effect directly in the 3D window.  
This feature allows faster and freer creation of patterns and prints.  

Next, let’s look at the optimization of the UV editor.  
From this version, you can quickly and accurately select versions based on the same property within the UV editor window.  
Multiple garments exist in this file.  
In the main menu, under Material > UV, click UV editor to open the window.  
In the UV editor window, you can see the pull chain versions.  
Hovering over the list displays purple options, including particle structure layer and material.  
Using material as an example, select the version and click it.  
All versions using the same material will be selected simultaneously in the UV editor.  
You can easily select versions, move to the target UV area, or directly bake the UV.  
The particle structure layer behaves similarly.  
Another added option: select all sewing versions, select the sleeve version of the chain, right-click.  
Clicking this option selects all chain versions at once.  
You can also use the shortcut Ctrl+Alt+A or double-click the version and select the sleeve version of the chain.  
This function is useful when adjusting all related versions of a specific version.  
With these functions, you can quickly and accurately group properties as needed, making UV baking more efficient.  

Next, improvements related to animation:  
After this update, you can apply keyframes to more properties, including pressure-resistant sewing needles, shrunk sheets, shape-adjusting sheets, and accessories.  
Usability of the animation editor is significantly improved.  
First, when setting keyframes, the animation editor opens automatically—no manual opening needed.  
This helps achieve a smoother and more intuitive workflow.  
Second, multiple functions simplify adding and editing cross-layer keyframes.  
You can create keyframes for multiple object layers in the scene.  

Using a costume as an example:  
On the animation editor timeline, add the keyframe position to the playhead.  
In the object layer list, use Ctrl or Shift to select multiple layers.  
You will see a new layer added in the toolbar’s automatic keyframe section, with an add keyframe icon.  
Click the icon to create keyframes for all selected layers simultaneously.  
Press and hold the icon to select the tool group.  
Click to create a layer for all objects.  
After clicking, all objects that can be keyed—costumes, virtual models, controllers, etc.—will be added to the animation editor.  
From the same tool group, choose to add keyframes for all layers.  
You can create keyframes for all object layers without further selection.  

Now, exploring new keyframe properties:  
You can create new keyframes by simply changing settings in the support menu.  
The switch and click button appearing in the upper-right corner are the animation editor keyframes.  
They provide new keyframes for all object layers.  
One keyframe is the active keyframe in play, which is essential for functionality.  
You can graph the keyframe from the snackbar by clicking the icon.  
Set key binding by clicking the icon again.  
In this mode, click the icon again to set the final keyframe.  
Complete the animation to adjust simulation quality.  
Cut to hand frame and adjust playback range.  
Click the recording icon in the toolbar.  
Play the animation after recording completes.  
You will see smooth pressure value changes in the 3D window.  
If you need to modify the pressure value, click the small triangle on the left side of the board to open detailed properties, modify the pressure value, and reset the keyframe.  
You can modify the ratio in the property editor or animation editor on the left side of the board.  
This affects the 3D window panel shrinkage effect.  

Regarding panel shape optimization:  
You can choose to activate shape optimization and adjust its strength parameters.  
The initial state is with shape solidification activated.  
At the 8th keyframe, shape solidification is activated.  
At the 24th keyframe, the strength of shape solidification is set to 100.  
You can see the final effect.  
About fake keyframes:  
Activation state adjustment is supported.  
Additionally, line length can be set as a keyframe.  
Regarding copy, you can freely set its weight change.  
The keyframe animation line now supports more properties.  
These updates make animation editing more accurate and performant.  
Try these new functions to create more exquisite and vivid animations.  

In the previous Clo version, when rendering a turntable image, if stopped halfway, rendering could not restart from the stopped frame.  
From this version, you can set start and end frames for rendering turntable images.  
Open the rendering window.  
In the Image/Video properties menu, switch to turntable image.  
After switching, you will see two new fields: start frame and end frame.  
Click to start rendering.  
If rendering stops, you can enter the starting frame, and rendering will restart from that frame.  
This update gives you better control over turntable rendering.  

We have released a new function for delay and cost savings.  
Combined with other data performance functions, users can now check workflow efficiency and current cost-saving status.  
First, go to the company layer settings page.  
Select Content > Workflow.  
Click the plus sign below to add a custom workflow label.  
Click the end state button to set the delivery period, determining the label that represents the workflow’s final step.  
You can click or unclick the checkbox.  
After setup, you can change the current workflow status label for each 3D file.  
For example, when a file is accepted by the buyer, you can change the label to the final draft approved status.  
Finally, click the data analytics icon in the upper right corner for delivery cycle analysis.  
For example, average delivery cycles and times show average consumption of each workflow stage.  
For example, you spent an average of 13 hours completing the first draft round.  
You can also filter selection results by category, such as clothing and men’s clothing.  
Click Apply to select.  
Scroll down to see the time spent on each file.  
Back in the studio, click the data savings icon in the upper right corner to calculate total cost savings in the studio.  
Cost savings are based on the number of versions and color counts per model.  
The default cost is user-defined.  
Scroll down to set custom cost definitions per file.  
For example, it usually costs $30 to produce one plus-size version.  
The system will automatically calculate current cost savings using the new data-saving tool.  
Users can automatically evaluate cost and efficiency.

chunks.title: CLO 2025.2 - Introduction to Other Features
chunks.content: # CLO 2025.2 - Introduction to Other Features This document details the new features, improvements, and updates introduced in CLO version 2025.2. It covers enhancements to the drawing library, shortcut customization, sewing and 2D tools, 3D garment editing, animation, rendering, data analytics, and compatibility improvements ensuring better workflow flexibility and efficiency. --- ## Drawing Library Updates: Floating and Docking Options This section explains the major update to the new drawing library interface, including floating and docking window options to improve workspace customization. - In version 2025.2, the new drawing library can now be used as either a floating window or docked to the side of the screen column. - By default, clicking the drawing library icon opens it as a floating window. - To dock the drawing library, click the docking icon in the upper right corner; it docks by default to the left side of the screen but can also be docked on the right side. - The window and property editor appear side by side when docked. - To restore the floating window, click the window icon in the upper right corner of the drawing library. - User docking settings are saved and automatically apply on the next software launch. - The old drawing library has been removed in this version, fully replaced by the new one. - This feature enables UI customization to suit different workflows. --- ## Shortcut Customization Enhancements This section covers updates to shortcut key management, including unlocking, searching, editing, and linking shortcuts with 2D codes. - A new shortcut unlocking feature is available in the User Customization window under the shortcut selection tab. - Users can search shortcuts by order name or shortcut key via keyword or full name input. - Pressing a keyboard shortcut highlights it for easy identification. - When customizing shortcuts, conflicts with default system shortcuts are warned; users can choose to replace conflicting shortcuts. - All shortcuts can now be viewed and edited directly in the 2D window. - Sewing line shortcuts are linked with codes to maintain structural consistency across all sizes. - Shortcut codes appear on the codeboard, automatically adapting their size for all garment sizes. - In the edit code tool, selected shortcuts can have their position adjusted via the property editor. - The "fixed size" option locks shortcut code positions to ensure consistent placement across sizes. - Length display lines show constant distances between shortcuts when switching sizes. - The lock position can toggle between start and end points, and numerical input can adjust distances. - Input values are based on machine code; prefixing a number with a comma reverses direction for a specific size. - Selecting "opposite direction" reverses all sizes. - Sewing lines for garments like chest coats and skirts remain perfectly aligned at cutouts across sizes, improving measurement accuracy and board consistency. --- ## Sticker Placement with 2D Measurement This section explains the updated sticker adjustment tool leveraging accurate 2D measurements for precise positioning.
chunks.content_description: CLO 2025.2 Overview of Other New Features! Join CLO technical experts to explore all the remaining feature enhancements in the new version, helping to elevate your design workflow to the next level!

chunks.title: CLO 2025.2 - Introduction to Other Features
chunks.content: - The lock position can toggle between start and end points, and numerical input can adjust distances. - Input values are based on machine code; prefixing a number with a comma reverses direction for a specific size. - Selecting "opposite direction" reverses all sizes. - Sewing lines for garments like chest coats and skirts remain perfectly aligned at cutouts across sizes, improving measurement accuracy and board consistency. --- ## Sticker Placement with 2D Measurement This section explains the updated sticker adjustment tool leveraging accurate 2D measurements for precise positioning. - The adjustment sticker tool allows users to select stickers for fine-tuning. - In the property editor, users can activate 2D measurement based on endpoints or outer lines. - Selecting the endpoint option displays a distance parameter next to the sticker within the sheet range. - Users can manually enter values to control the distance between sticker endpoints or outer lines. - For back positioning, the outer line measurement option can be activated and set. - This allows precise sticker placement to meet process unit requirements. - The update enhances positioning accuracy, ensuring design control. --- ## Fixing Needle Tool Improvements This section outlines the enhanced selection and deletion options for fixing needles on 3D garments. - Users can now delete all fixing needles on a selected sheet, instead of only deleting selected needles or all needles on the entire garment. - Fixing needles can be added randomly on different sheets using the fixing needle tool. - Right-clicking a fixing needle on a sheet offers an option to delete all fixing needles on that specific sheet. - This provides greater editing flexibility for 3D garment creation. - Double-clicking a fixing needle selects all needles on the same sheet; pressing Delete removes them. - Previous functionality to delete all fixing needles remains available. - This sheet-by-sheet deletion avoids unnecessary removal of needles across the entire garment. --- ## Sewing Function Activation Control This section details the update allowing users to activate or deactivate sewing lines for more flexible garment design. - The sewing tool now includes an activation toggle in the property editor. - Users can add sewing lines (e.g., neckline, armhole) and then activate or deactivate them without deleting. - The function applies both on the garment and virtual model. - Users can simulate with sewing lines activated or deactivated to preview different states. - This flexibility improves sewing function usability compared to previous versions where sewing lines persisted unless deleted. --- ## Software Model Simulation on GPU This section describes the extension of software model simulation support to GPU mode to improve performance. - Previously, only CPU simulation supported software model simulation. - Version 2025.2 enables software model simulation in GPU simulation mode. - Users activate this in the property editor by enabling the software model simulation option for the virtual model. - The 3D window displays a software model simulation icon when active. - Switching between simulation modes retains the software model simulation.

chunks.content: --- ## Software Model Simulation on GPU This section describes the extension of software model simulation support to GPU mode to improve performance. - Previously, only CPU simulation supported software model simulation. - Version 2025.2 enables software model simulation in GPU simulation mode. - Users activate this in the property editor by enabling the software model simulation option for the virtual model. - The 3D window displays a software model simulation icon when active. - Switching between simulation modes retains the software model simulation. - Recording software model animation in the animation editor is faster. - This feature is supported only on Windows systems with NVIDIA GPUs. - The update provides a smoother and faster simulation experience. --- ## Custom Hat Configurations This section explains the new capability to create and save customized hat configurations for virtual models. - Users can access the virtual model menu and select "Customized Configuration." - A new "Hat" configuration type is available. - OBJ files can be imported as hat versions. - Multiple hat versions can be selected and saved as a customized configuration. - Saved hats can be freely added to other projects. - This expands customization possibilities for virtual model accessories. --- ## MetaHuman Virtual Model Import This section covers importing MetaHuman models into CLO as virtual models for enhanced realism and compatibility. - MetaHuman models in DNA format can be imported from the main menu. - DNA files must be stored alongside other postage files to ensure correct skin presentation. - In the MetaHuman DNA import window, users select body and head files via the File plus icon. - Import settings include unit and proportion adjustments. - By default, arrangement points are auto-added and test fitting created; these can be disabled for manual setup. - After import, MetaHuman models appear in the workspace as virtual models. - The 3D vertical menu allows modification of surface types and displaying arrangement points. - This supports self-defined role models from MetaHuman Creator, improving interoperability with Unreal Engine. --- ## Pull Chain Symmetry and Appearance Optimization This section explains improvements in pull chain copying, activation, and visual behavior. - Pull chains can be copied to symmetrical versions via right-click and selecting "Copy to version with symmetrical modification." - The copied pull chain retains the same material and specifications as the original. - Pull chains can be activated with the version or back-activated, maintaining their state when switching versions. - Back-activation synchronizes pull chain states to simplify operations. - These updates improve efficiency in creating symmetrical pull chains and streamline workflow. --- ## Text Rotation in Text Editor This section highlights the new feature allowing text rotation in the text editor for pattern and print design. - Text can be rotated horizontally or vertically by selecting it and clicking the corresponding rotate button. - The effect is visible directly in the 3D window. - This eliminates manual rotation steps and speeds up design creation.
